dossier.mechanism: AppMeta Pulse turns Apple's App Store Connect API into a ten-second morning read of yesterday's proceeds, subscriptions, trials, refunds and downloads across every app you ship. It monitors by construction: there is no code for builds, pricing or metadata, and its only writes are review replies you send and analytics report requests. The .p8 key stays in Keychain and every query goes straight to Apple.
dossier.audienceScene: An indie iOS developer or small-studio founder with several live apps, 7 to 9 am, phone in one hand and coffee in the other at a kitchen table or café counter (or at a departure gate at the end of the week). They open the app the morning Apple's next-day Sales and Trends numbers land and decide in seconds whether yesterday needs attention. On desktop they are at the Mac and need to get the app onto their iPhone.
dossier.culturalHome: The indie Apple developer scene: App Store Connect Sales and Trends and the monthly financial reports, Apple's own vocabulary (proceeds, units, the 15% Small Business Program), App Store Top Grossing charts, Home Screen widgets, WWDC, revenue-screenshot posts on Mastodon and Bluesky, indie podcasts. Also the older rituals the morning check comes from: the newspaper markets page over breakfast, the instrument you read but cannot adjust, the scoreboard read from the stands.
dossier.mustProve: In one viewport: what it shows (portfolio proceeds, subscriptions, refunds and downloads in Apple's terms, at a glance); that it cannot change anything in App Store Connect except review replies you send; that nothing is collected and queries go straight to Apple; the real price (free trial, from $0.99/mo, $8.99/yr, $17.99 lifetime); and a working install path (the official badge, plus the QR on desktop).
dossier.categoryDefault: A dark indigo-to-black SaaS analytics landing page: glowing cyan-violet line chart, floating iPhone showing the dashboard, KPI tiles (big number over a small label), feature card grid, three equal pricing cards, testimonial carousel. In effect the app icon's palette blown up to page scale, the AppStats / Appfigures / RevenueCat marketing pattern.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Apple-keynote minimalism: a white page, a giant grotesk headline, one centred floating iPhone, generous whitespace, a single blue link. Or the incumbent's cream editorial look.
dossier.literalReading: 'Pulse' read literally is a heartbeat or ECG trace on a vital-signs monitor, and 'dashboard' is a car instrument cluster. Both are the rut, and the ECG collides with Observa's health world. Neither is among the seven.

candidates.name: The morning markets page
candidates.why: The app's own word is 'portfolio' (ten-plus uses) and its ritual is 'coffee, app, number'. Before the web, that ritual was reading yesterday's closing prices over breakfast. Carries the mechanism as listings: each app is a holding with yesterday's figures and the change against the previous period, the 'How to read the tables' key is Apple's vocabulary (proceeds vs sales), and the Reader Services box is the install panel.

candidates.name: The trade chart page
candidates.why: Indie developers live by the App Store's Top Grossing charts, and Billboard's Hot 100 and the weekend box-office grosses are the trade-paper form of that obsession. Carries per-app contribution ranked by proceeds, with THIS WEEK / LAST WEEK / CHANGE columns as period-over-period movement. Weakness: it ranks your own apps against each other, which the app never does.

candidates.name: The seven-day recorder chart
candidates.why: Barograph and strip-chart recorder paper (printed blue rulings, violet aniline pen ink that matches the icon's own violet, a red event pen) is the classic record that can only record. Carries the 7D default view, this week against the previous week as two pens (the app's Period Comparison), Apple's once-a-day cadence as daily steps, and 'Controls: none' printed in the chart's label block.

candidates.name: The Home Screen Smart Stack
candidates.why: Every iOS developer knows their own Home Screen by heart. The journal calls the widget the app's highest-engagement surface, and 6.png shows the 7-Day Dashboard widgets. Carries the glance as real widget sizes and the dock as the sticky download bar. Weakness: it is nearly a picture of the product, sits close to the dark-indigo category default, and would likely converge with Soon's widget world.

candidates.name: The hand-hung ballpark scoreboard
candidates.why: Wrigley's and Fenway's green steel boards are read from the stands at a glance and cannot be touched by the crowd. Carries the portfolio as a line score (the per-app rows from 2.png, summing to the 992,55 € total in 1.png), the price as hung plates, and the ball-strike-out lamps recast as Build / Pricing / Metadata lamps that are not wired.

candidates.name: The sealed utility meter
candidates.why: A meter is read but never adjusted, it is closed with a tamper seal, and a reading is present minus previous. Carries read-only by construction and the period comparison. Weakness: it holds one number, not a portfolio, and sits next to Allpaid's bills world.

candidates.name: The boxed Mac software carton
candidates.why: Before the web, Mac software came shrink-wrapped, with a system-requirements side panel, a feature back panel and a price sticker. Flattened as a dieline it carries the price sticker, an 'in the box / not in the box' panel (no build, pricing or metadata controls) and the QR in the UPC position. Weakness: it does not carry the glance itself, and it would fit any app in the catalogue.

styles.label: Seven-Day Chart
styles.lineage: Short & Mason and Negretti & Zambra seven-day barograph charts, and Esterline Angus / Leeds & Northrup strip-chart recorders: printed blue rulings, day divisions, violet aniline pen ink, a red event pen, and the printed label block in the chart's corner.
styles.thesis: The page is one roll of recorder chart paper fed past a fixed pen. A week of portfolio proceeds is traced in violet against last week in graphite, recorded by an instrument whose label block reads 'Controls: none'. It refuses the dark gradient dashboard of floating KPI tiles.
styles.scene: An indie developer at a kitchen table or café counter in 7 to 9 am daylight, phone in hand, reading what Apple published overnight. That means light chart paper, one scheme (color-scheme: light).

styles.navigation: Nav lives on the chart's printed top edge: wordmark plus five anchor links in B612. On mobile an 'Index' button opens the chart legend as a ruled list. From 1100px wide, the right-edge event channel doubles as the jump nav (jump_nav: true): every section has a red event tick with its printed name, and the tick for the section in view turns violet. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: Read the pen, a reading cursor. Each day band is a focusable row; arrow keys move between rows. Hover, tap or focus draws a 1px violet hairline across both traces and prints that day's reading and the same day last week in the left margin (about 40 lines of vanilla JS reading data attributes that mirror the server-rendered table). Without JS, the readings column is a real <table> printed beside the bands, so every value is visible. With reduced motion, the cursor jumps without easing and the trace is already inked.
styles.motionGrammar: Ink, not glide. On first view the violet trace inks downward from the pen once (SVG stroke-dashoffset, 900ms, linear). Event ticks appear in place with an opacity step and no movement. The pen carriage travels 8px into place in 160ms. Nothing fades in on scroll, and no counters run. With prefers-reduced-motion, everything is pre-inked and the carriage appears without travel.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support, the /api-access/ methodology page and the three alternatives pages keep the printed top edge, with a label block as the page header (Title · App · Last updated · back to /apps/appmeta-pulse/). Rulings recede to the margins; a 68ch unruled paper column carries Atkinson 18px/1.6 body-ink text, with H2s in B612 700 chart-blue. Privacy data lists are set as a printed legend table. Alternatives pages show the head-to-head as a two-pen record: one row per fact (monthly, yearly, lifetime, what the privacy label declares, notifications/widgets, platforms), with AppMeta Pulse in violet ink and the competitor in graphite, followed by 'Pick … if' columns and the FAQ as the operator's log. The support page is a label block with email, response time and a ruled 'what to include' checklist.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. The grid is CSS. Traces are inline SVG from illustrative values traced off 1.png and 5.png and labelled as such. The nib is a three-path inline SVG. Existing screenshots, icon and QR cover the rest.
styles.risk: If the label block and the two traces are weak, chart paper reads as generic graph paper or an engineering costume. Time running down the page is unfamiliar, and the illustrative week could be mistaken for live data, so the labels must be explicit. The grid behind type has to be suppressed under every text column to hold contrast.
styles.memoryTest: A page made of chart paper: a violet pen line tracing a week of App Store proceeds against last week's grey line, a label block that said 'Controls: none', and the download badge riding on the pen carriage.

type.rationale: League Gothic revives Alternate Gothic No. 1, the tall condensed headline gothic of American newspapers; it sets the section flag, the banner and the section heads. Libre Franklin revives Franklin Gothic, the newspaper's workhorse sans, used here for body text, datelines and agate stock tables. All sans and all roman: no italic display serif and no tracked mono labels, which keeps the page out of the broadsheet-editorial cliché. About 48 KB.

styles.navigation: An 'Inside' index sits in the flag like a front-page index box: Listings · Key · Rates · Disclosures · Letters · Column. On mobile, the 'Inside' button opens it as an agate list under the flag. A folio line at the foot of each section ('AppMeta Pulse · Listings') doubles as a back-to-top link. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: Read the key: cross-highlighting between the 'How to read these tables' key and the listings. Each key term links to its column or row id. Tapping, hovering or focusing a term swipes the highlighter across the term and the matching table column (vanilla JS toggles a class; a CSS background-size swipe runs 220ms). Without JS, the links jump by fragment and CSS :target highlights the column header and the definition. With reduced motion, the highlight fills instantly.
styles.motionGrammar: Print holds still; only the highlighter moves. It swipes left to right (background-size 0 to 100%, 220ms ease-out) on hover, focus or :target, and the sticky flag strip drops 6px in 140ms. No scroll reveals and no counters, because the numbers are printed. With prefers-reduced-motion, swipes become instant fills.
styles.readModeVariant: The privacy page becomes 'Disclosures': section flag, banner title, a single 66ch column of Libre Franklin 18px with League Gothic subheads, data lists as agate tables, and the transparency row as a boxed fact panel linking /transparency/. The support page becomes 'Reader Services': a halftone box with email and response time, and 'what to include' as an agate checklist. The /api-access/ page is set as a markets explainer with endpoint tables in agate. Alternatives pages become 'Comparable listings': a head-to-head agate table (for AppStats: $0.99 vs $2.99/mo, $8.99 vs $19.99/yr, $17.99 vs $49.99 lifetime, privacy label declares none vs usage data and diagnostics, notifications and widgets). The winning cell is highlighted for whichever side wins it, AppStats' wins included. Then the article runs in one column, followed by the 'Letters' FAQ.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Halftone, rules and highlighter are CSS; screenshots, QR and icon already exist.
styles.risk: This is the most familiar of the three: newspaper and editorial layouts are a frequent 'creative' answer and sit next to the broadsheet-editorial cluster. It has to stay sans and roman, with the highlighter used only for real marks. The studio's own Read world may also go editorial, which would blur this microsite's identity. Dense agate tables are tiring on a phone. The stock-market framing must never imply investment returns, so every column is labelled in Apple's terms.
styles.memoryTest: It was a morning newspaper's market page: my apps were the listings, the key at the bottom explained proceeds vs sales, and the download sat in a yellow-highlighted subscription box.

type.display: Archivo 800 at wdth 125 (Expanded) for plate numerals, board lettering and headings (@fontsource-variable/archivo, wdth file about 90 KB, which also covers the text width)

type.utility: None. Every figure uses Archivo tabular numerals on plates.
type.rationale: Archivo revives late-19th-century American grotesques, the era of ballpark sign painting. Its expanded heavy numerals fill square plates the way painted plate numerals do, and the same alphabet at normal width carries the reading text: one sign-painter's alphabet in two widths. It is neither condensed nor mono, so it does not echo the other two styles. About 90 KB.

styles.navigation: Painted links run across the board's nameplate band: Score · Lamps · Price · Questions · Privacy, in Archivo 600 15px white with an amber underline on hover or focus. On mobile, a 'Menu' plate opens a full-width list of painted name plates. On desktop, the jump nav (jump_nav: true) is a row of unnumbered section name plates that sticks under the nameplate band like the board's inning header. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: Test the lamps. A 'Test the lamps' plate on the lamp panel runs the board's lamp test: REVIEW REPLIES and ANALYTICS REQUESTS light in sequence, while BUILDS, PRICING and METADATA stay dark and their labels print 'No code for this', linking to /apps/appmeta-pulse/api-access/. The fact comes from the FAQ and the methodology page. About 25 lines of vanilla JS toggle classes, and the button announces its result through aria-live. Without JS, the lamps are server-rendered in their true states (two lit, three dark) with the full labels visible. With reduced motion, the test lights both lamps at once, with no sequence.
styles.motionGrammar: Manual, never electronic. When the line score first enters view, the plates arrive with a short hinge flip (rotateX -90° to 0°, 180ms, 50ms stagger, once); the real numerals are already in the DOM. Lamps switch on with a 120ms fill change inside the lamp only, with no outer glow. The bottom rail travels 8px. No counters and no scroll scrubbing. With prefers-reduced-motion, plates and lamps are simply in place.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support, /api-access/ and the three alternatives pages keep the green board as the frame. Each has the nameplate band, the page title painted in Archivo Expanded 800, and one row of word plates (DATA COLLECTED: NONE · TRACKING: NO · ACCOUNT: NONE). These are words on plates, not big-number tiles. The reading column is an enamel scorecard panel (#F7F8F4, board-green text, Archivo 18px/1.6, 68ch) set into the board. Alternatives pages become a two-team line score: rows for AppMeta Pulse and the competitor, columns $/MO · $/YR · LIFETIME · PRIVACY LABEL · WIDGETS, with real values from each alternatives page hung as plates. The competitor's wins are shown as lit too. 'Pick … if' columns and the FAQ follow on the scorecard. The support page is a scorecard panel with email, response time and what to include.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Plates, lamps, seams and panels are CSS. Line-score figures are the numbers printed in 2.png and 1.png/5.png, labelled as such. Badge, QR, icon and screenshots already exist.
styles.risk: A ballpark board can read as gamified, or as American-sports-specific to a global indie audience and a calm brand. A drenched dark green is heavy for long reading, hence the scorecard panel. A 'score' framing can imply your apps compete with each other. The plate grid needs strict tabular alignment at 390px or it collapses into a tile grid.
styles.memoryTest: A green ballpark scoreboard with my apps' numbers hung on plates, and a lamp panel where Builds, Pricing and Metadata never lit up because they aren't wired.

canon: Canon (the standing exit, never recommended): the category's SaaS analytics landing page played straight. An indigo-to-black gradient taken from the icon, a floating iPhone showing the 7-day dashboard, three KPI tiles, a feature card grid, three equal pricing cards with Lifetime highlighted, and an FAQ accordion, in an SF-like grotesk at the craft level of Apple's own product pages.
notes: The roll ran degraded (roll service unreachable; no catalog challengers and no quality-bar boards). The dealt index binds anyway. Seed key 6ff8c40b, assigned 3, re-roll 1 dealt 5 (distinct, so no further re-roll). Neither dealt index is 1, so B is my top candidate as IMPECCABLE’S PICK. Styles split world, topology and light: A is light chart paper, Full palette, with time running down a strip and the sticky bar as the pen carriage. B is light newsprint, Restrained with one highlighter, on a 12-column broadsheet grid of listings. C is a Drenched dark board green, with plates and a lamp panel on one board face. Fonts were verified on Fontsource (b612 400/700, b612-mono 400, atkinson-hyperlegible-next variable, league-gothic variable wdth, libre-franklin variable, archivo variable wdth+wght), and every style stays at or under about 90 KB. Things the owner should know: (1) the 6.png caption says 'Same dashboard on Mac' but the image is the Home Screen 7-Day Dashboard widgets; fix the caption or the file. (2) platforms is ['iOS'] while the copy claims iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro; styles state 'iPhone · iPad · Mac' as the copy does. Confirm the schema value. (3) The journal says the free tier covers one app, but front matter says free trial; styles use the front matter. (4) No how_it_works, so no HowTo steps exist to render; the A/C 'wiring' and 'lamp' sections come from the api-access facts instead. (5) All portfolio figures are the developer's own screenshot data and are labelled illustrative everywhere. (6) Widgets are not claimed as a differentiator, because the AppStats page concedes AppStats is stronger there. (7) B's editorial world may collide with whatever the studio's Read world becomes; check before choosing it.
